prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
U0098: Manual coordination would employ the same methods currently used for reroutes, but would be informed by DRAW weather conflict prediction and integrated trial planning capability.
U0099: Integrated trial planning would allow each facility to review both weather and schedule impact of proposed reroutes.
U0100: Thus, the number of iterations on a viable reroute may be reduced and the efficacy of reroutes in actually avoiding convective weather would improve.
U0101: Due to the complexity of manually coordinating operational constraints across multiple facilities in real-time, this method would be used primarily for groups of aircraft and be relatively infrequent for individual flights (likely limited to acute situations or at operator request, time permitting).
U0102: Electronic approval requests (APREQs) could replace many telephone calls to expedite the approval process and allow TMCs to conduct other tasks while awaiting approval for route modifications outside their airspace.
U0103: Using APREQs, a TMC could build a trial plan reroute that includes changes beyond the boundaries of their airspace, and await electronic approval of those changes.
U0104: If the proposed reroute was approved by the other involved TMU(s) without modification, the reroute would be implemented as originally proposed.
U0105: If additional changes are required by other TMUs, those changes could be coordinated with additional APREQs or (if sufficiently complex) via telephone.
U0106: The APREQ approval chain for DRAW reroutes are only intended to facilitate coordination and is not intended as a safeguard against reroutes without proper coordination; the facility with track control of a flight may issue a reroute without proper coordination in the current system, and DRAW is not intended to change that capability. 4.3.2 Reroute Implementation Successful coordination of a DRAW trial plan results in a pending flight plan amendment (or group of amendments) that is either explicitly or implicitly approved by the proper authority within the TMU of each involved facility.
U0107: Implementation of this would be accomplished in one of three ways: 1) current practice (voice implementation), 2) Airborne Reroute (ABRR), or 3) a combination of 1) and 2).
U0108: Lacking integrated ABRR capability (with TBFM or via a TFMS connection), a pending flight plan amendment would be communicated by voice to sector controller (directly or through the area supervisor) for clearance to the flight crew and entry into ERAM.
U0109: Because of the requirement for entry into ERAM and because of the potential for error in communication and readback of route amendments, it is desirable that reroutes are not overly complex (i.e., routes should avoid use of Fix-Radial-Distance waypoints if possible).
U0110: In a more advanced implementation, TBFM could send a reroute directly to ERAM via the ABRR interface even across facilities since, presumably, a pending amendment has been fully coordinated and approved.
U0111: It is unclear, though, if this use of ABRR (direct to ERAM from a system other than TFMS) is envisioned or advisable at this point in time.
U0112: More likely in an ABRR environment is that some mix of voice communication of reroutes (or electronic log messages to those with access to intrafacility ABRR) and ABRR implementation of reroutes within a single facility will be employed.
U0113: This solution would reduce systems integration requirements, instead relying on telephone calls and electronic messages to employ existing reroute methods. 4.4 DRAW USE CASES DRAW assists traffic managers by continuously evaluating flights to identify opportunities to improve arrival traffic flow.
U0114: Use cases for the two types of DRAW route advisories are described below. 4.4.1 Time-Saving Route to Alternate Meter Fix Use Case Name: DRAW Advisory for Time-Saving Route to Alternate Meter Fix or STAR transition route Summary: The DRAW system receives current arrival flight plan trajectories and analyzes them for opportunities to save time.
U0115: Note: DRAW advisories are proposed for airborne arrival flights only.
U0116: Pre-conditions: Data from external sources must be acquired to define the constraints and the filed flight plans:  ERAM: Flight plan and tracks from home and first-tier adjacent Centers  (At least) hourly wind updates (e.g., NOAA Rapid Refresh)  Current and forecasted weather data (e.g., CIWS)  Polygon-based weather avoidance fields (e.g., CWAM)  TBFM: metering data such as metering status, scheduled times of arrival (STAs) for metered flights, schedule delay, metering constraint definitions (and rules for applying them) Trigger Events: New or periodically updated flight track information Nominal Actions: 1.
